entries.title: A page for every game
entries.body: Every game in all nine leagues now has a page: the final score next to what each side's shots were worth, a score race, both shot maps and every player's line, plus a list of each league-season's games. Field goals are priced with the shot-making model and free throws at the shooter's season rate, so the shots' worth is what the attempts were worth, not a corrected score. It is not a luck number either: the actual margin moves only 0.44 points per point of expected margin in the NBA, because misses bring putbacks and trailing teams shoot more. A "these shots win N in 100" figure was built and failed its calibration test, so it is not shown. Greek Basket League games carry no date, since its dates are estimated, and games whose play-by-play does not add up to the final are left out and counted.

entries.title: The NBA back to 1997-98
entries.body: Twenty-three more NBA seasons, 1997-98 to 2019-20, with all three lenses, teams and, from 2003-04, referees. The archive is built with the same models as today, each season's trained on its six nearest seasons so a 1998 shot is priced on late-1990s basketball, and it loads only when a page asks for it. Players with archive seasons get their whole careers. Before the 2004-05 hand-check change foul-drawing leans toward tall players, because post-ups drew fouls and a shot-location baseline cannot see a post-up; the methodology page has the numbers. 1996-97 is left out: its shot locations are coded differently and skew its zone model. Building it also fixed shots missing from four current-era seasons: about 1,800 a season had no court location and dropped out of shot value.

entries.title: Referees, measured against the expected whistle
entries.body: Each official is now measured against the expected whistle of the games they worked: what those players would draw from where they shot, each at their own foul-drawing rate in their other games. One season of an official turns out to be mostly noise (about a third signal in the NBA), so every figure is pulled toward the league by how much of it is noise and shown with a 90% range, and profiles lead with the career figure. The quarter and close-game splits stay, drawn against what the official's overall level predicts, because individual leans by quarter or game script do not repeat. Greek Basket League officials, listed in Greek in some games and Latin in others, are no longer merged into one.

entries.title: Explore: plot any two numbers
entries.body: A chart builder at /explore. Put any two of twelve published numbers on the axes, for one league or all nine, and read the trend and its correlation off the chart. Colour the dots by an over-expected figure, filter by position or possessions, mark players by name, and tap a dot for his numbers. Across leagues it ranks each player within his own league, since over-expected figures are measured against the league they were earned in. The link carries the whole chart, and the chart downloads as an image.

entries.title: The front page leads with this week
entries.body: The homepage now opens on the week's hottest and coldest shooting games across every league, with faces on the season's leaders. Player pages open on shot value, the headline number, with the scouting report linked at the top. On phones, season pickers are a compact menu instead of a row that wrapped.

entries.title: One-page scouting reports
entries.body: Every player page links to a one-page scouting report laid out for A4: the season's key numbers with percentiles, shot diet against the league, the five closest profiles in other leagues, the EuroLeague projection for domestic players, and every qualified season. Save it as a PDF from the browser.

entries.title: Same profile, other leagues
entries.body: Every player page now lists the players in the other eight leagues who play most like him: where they shoot from, how much they shoot, and how they convert and draw fouls against their own league. Only current players are listed. Tested on players who played EuroLeague and a domestic league in the same season, the profile puts a player's own EuroLeague season in the top five of about 147 EuroLeague players 46% of the time.

entries.title: What he would shoot in EuroLeague
entries.body: Player pages in Liga ACB, Lega Basket Serie A, the Basketball Bundesliga, ABA Liga and the Greek Basket League now project the player's shot-making in EuroLeague. His domestic figure is trusted in proportion to his attempts, then moved by his league's step to EuroLeague, measured on 576 players who played both in the same season. Tested on seasons it never saw, it beats both assuming he shoots the same and assuming a league-average EuroLeague shooter, and the range shown is as wide as one EuroLeague season of shots really is.

entries.title: This week in shooting
entries.body: A weekly post: the hottest and coldest shooting games of each Monday-to-Sunday week across eight leagues, ranked by points scored from the field against what those shots were worth. One game of the week across every league, then each league's top three each way, with a share card per week. The archive starts with the 2025-26 seasons. The Greek Basket League is left out because its feed carries no game dates.

entries.title: Foul-drawing now measured against where a player shoots
entries.body: FTAOE's expectation used to come from game context (clock, score, home court, opponent and officiating crew). That explained about 1% of the difference between players, so the number tracked the raw free-throw rate almost exactly (r 0.995 in the NBA) and leaned on height. Expected free throws now come from shot location: each attempt at the rim, in the paint, from mid-range or from three is valued at that season's league free throws per attempt in its zone, with fouled misses counted back in. In the NBA the new figure correlates 0.70 with the raw rate and 0.05 with height, repeats at 0.78 from one season to the next, and agrees at 0.85 with an independent version built from tracking data. Points over expected now uses it for its free-throw half. Team and referee views keep the context model.

entries.title: Weekly updates again, and the 2026-27 season
entries.body: Data refreshes every Monday again, now for all nine leagues. 2026-27 is in the season picker for the NBA and seven European leagues, and becomes each league's default once enough players qualify. The WNBA rolls over to its complete 2026 season. The Greek Basket League stays at 2025-26: its game ids cannot be listed while a season is under way.

entries.title: Glossary, and headshots for six more leagues
entries.body: Added a glossary page for every quantity the site measures, each with its unit, its real range and what it does not tell you. Player photos now resolve for EuroLeague, EuroCup, Liga ACB, Lega Basket Serie A, ABA Liga and the Greek Basket League, taking faces from 743 to 2,799 of 3,301 player pages.

entries.title: League, season and metric moved into the URL
entries.body: Every league, season and lens combination is now its own address, so a specific leaderboard can be linked and shared. The old bare paths redirect permanently. Every page also ships its content as HTML, so it is readable without JavaScript.

entries.title: Compare caught up to the player page
entries.body: Compare became a top-level section and gained the player card's four lenses, a head-to-head stat table, a shared shot-diet court and trailing form on one axis. NBA and WNBA player photos added.

entries.title: Player page reshaped around defence
entries.body: Defence became a fourth lens on the player page, showing D-RAPM with its interval against the season's qualified field. The sample-reliability and lineup-impact panels were removed.

entries.title: League became the team hub
entries.body: Team shot value and shot-making joined free throws on the league page, alongside the three defence pillars and clutch decision-making. Positive now reads warm in every league.

entries.title: Clutch decisions and team defence
entries.body: Two layers added: the end-game two-versus-three choice scored on expectation at the moment of the decision, and team defence in three pillars ordered by measured reliability. The player version of team defence was built and rejected at 0.348 split-half reliability.

entries.title: Lineups and RAPM
entries.body: Regularized adjusted plus-minus per player-season, plus five-man lineups measured against the sum of their parts. Reported honestly: RAPM beats a sum-of-parts baseline out of sample in all six seasons, but lineup synergy does not persist.

entries.title: EuroCup and the WNBA
entries.body: Two leagues added, taking the site to nine.

entries.title: Greek Basket League and ABA Liga
entries.body: Two more leagues. Liga Basket Serie A coordinates were also corrected: they are true-court and flip at halftime, which had put roughly 40% of its three-pointers in the backcourt.

entries.title: Lega Basket Serie A and Basketball Bundesliga
entries.body: Two leagues added. Bundesliga starts at 2023-24 because earlier seasons did not tag the shooter on missed shots, which makes per-player shot value impossible.

entries.title: NBA, EuroLeague and Liga ACB on one site
entries.body: The first combined release: one site, three leagues, a league toggle that reskins the interface and swaps the player database.
